title: Australian Centre for Disease Control (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2025
short_title: Australian Centre for Disease Control (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would transfer selected public health functions and records to the Australian Centre for Disease Control (CDC), supporting its establishment under companion legislation.

Its director-general would take responsibility for listed human diseases, national surveillance functions, the occupational respiratory disease registry and regulation of security-sensitive biological agents under existing laws.
Most human biosecurity functions would remain with the health department, and the substantive amendments would start with the companion legislation establishing the new centre.
changes: The national contact point for communication with the World Health Organization would move to the CDC director-general.
The health department secretary would replace the Commonwealth Chief Medical Officer as Director of Human Biosecurity.
The legislation establishing the Australian National Preventative Health Agency would be repealed.
Information protected under the CDC legislation would be exempt from disclosure under freedom of information law.
summary.affected: The Australian CDC and its Director-General, the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, the Commonwealth Chief Medical Officer and the Secretary, and people whose protected information is held are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: Supported the Australian Centre for Disease Control bills, arguing they provide independent, evidence-driven public health leadership with published advice, expert oversight, privacy protections and limits on coercive data powers, while urging sustained funding, staffing and broader responsibilities for chronic disease and climate-related health risks.

speeches.speaker: Sam Birrell
speeches.brief: Argued that the Australian Centre for Disease Control bills require fuller parliamentary scrutiny, consultation and inquiry, citing concerns about transferred powers, the chief medical officer's role, freedom of information, privacy and data sharing.
